title: UTC-aligned session timeline: SSH success, flagged sudo session, systemd state change
event_type: Threat-hunting timeline visualization — three-event session chain (sshd -> sudo -> systemd), synthetic positive-finding example from part 34 section 10.8

callouts.explanation: A single first-attempt success with no preceding failure burst satisfies the 'valid credentials' half of the hunt's hypothesis — this is not a brute-force compromise.
TTY=pts/2 present against an account with a zero-interactive-history baseline is the specific anomaly DET-34-01 is built to catch.
Linux telemetry has no native session-linking field like a Windows Logon ID, so this join is an explicit (account, host, time-proximity) judgment call that a second reviewer must be able to check.
The service restart immediately following the anomalous sudo session is the 'did something with it' step that completes the pivot chain from credential use to actionable lead.

note: CONCEPTUAL — an illustrative reconstruction of the synthetic three-event session chain described in section 10.8, laid out as a generic UTC-aligned timeline; it is not a captured screenshot of any real SIEM product interface.
